subtopics.title: LEADS Index Basics
subtopics.summary: LEADS stands for Logistics Ease Across Different States and is India's national index for benchmarking logistics performance across States and UTs. It was launched in 2018 and draws inspiration from the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index. The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade prepares the LEADS Report, and the 7th LEADS 2025 Report introduced a four-tier classification in place of the earlier three-tier model.
facts: LEADS stands for Logistics Ease Across Different States.
LEADS is India's National Index benchmarking logistics performance across States and UTs.
LEADS was launched in 2018.
LEADS draws inspiration from the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index.
The LEADS Report is prepared by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (Ministry of Commerce and Industry).
The Department released the 7th LEADS 2025 Report.
The 2025 edition introduced a four-tier classification system replacing the earlier three-tier model.
States and UTs are evaluated across key logistics parameters, including infrastructure, service quality and regulatory environment.
Data-driven logistics reforms are one of the evaluated parameters.
LEAPS stands for Logistics Excellence, Advancement and Performance Shield.

subtopics.title: State and UT Categories in LEADS 2025
subtopics.summary: The LEADS 2025 edition sorts States and UTs into four categories: Exemplars, High Performers, Accelerators and Growth-Seekers. Each entry is also tagged as Coastal, Landlocked, North-East (N-E) or UT. Some States and UTs moved from earlier labels such as Achiever or Fast Mover into the new categories.
facts: Exemplars (4): Tamil Nadu (Coastal), Uttar Pradesh (Landlocked), Mizoram (N-E), Delhi (UTs).
Uttar Pradesh achieved Exemplar status after being categorised as an Achiever from 2022 to 2024.
High Performers (11): Gujarat (Coastal), Haryana (Landlocked), Tripura (N-E), J&K (UTs).
J&K improved from Fast Mover in 2024 to High Performer in 2025.
Accelerators (17) include Andhra Pradesh (Coastal), Punjab (Landlocked) and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (UTs).
Growth-Seekers (4): West Bengal (Coastal), Rajasthan (Landlocked), Sikkim (N-E), Andaman and Nicobar Islands (UTs).
Regional tags used in the report: Coastal, Landlocked, N-E (North-East) and UTs.

subtopics.title: Logistics Sector Initiatives
subtopics.summary: Several government initiatives support India's logistics sector, including the National Logistics Policy 2022 and PM GatiShakti. The National Logistics Policy aims to lower logistics costs to levels on par with other developed countries. Other programmes focus on road connectivity, port-led development and digital e-way bills.
facts: National Logistics Policy 2022 aims to lower the cost of logistics to be on par with other developed countries.
Logistics costs in India remain relatively high at around 7.97% of GDP.
PM GatiShakti National Master Plan 2021 promotes integrated infrastructure planning across roads, railways, ports, airports and logistics networks.
Logistic Efficiency Enhancement Programme aims to enhance freight speed, reduce costs and improve tracking through technological and infrastructure upgrades.
Bharatmala Pariyojana aims to improve road connectivity across India.
Sagarmala Programme focuses on port-led development and boosts coastal shipping efficiency.
E-Way Bill System mandates digital bills for goods, easing inter-state transport.
India recorded exports of $863 billion in FY 2025-26 against a target of $1 trillion for the current year.

subtopics.title: Dedicated Freight Corridors
subtopics.summary: Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFCs) are exclusive freight routes built for double-stack and heavy-haul trains to carry goods at high capacity and speed. They are implemented by DFCCIL under the Ministry of Railways, with the objective of reducing logistics costs below 10 per cent. The Western DFC has improved port access and lowered transit times, although delays in its final section added to project costs.
facts: DFCs feature exclusive freight tracks for double-stack and heavy-haul trains with high capacity and speed.
The implementing agency is the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India (DFCCIL), under the Ministry of Railways.
The DFC objective is to reduce logistics costs below 10% as per the National Logistics Policy.
As per the National Rail Plan, DFCs aim to boost rail freight's share to 45% by 2030.
North-South DFC (Vijayawada-Itarsi) is 975 km long.
East Coast DFC (Kharagpur-Vijayawada) is 1115 km long.
EDFC is operational.
WDFC has improved port access and lowered transit times.
Delays in completing the final section of WDFC resulted in additional project costs.
DFCs lower logistics costs, generated jobs, attracted investments and contributed to Indian Railways' revenue growth (FY 2018-19 to FY 2022-23).

subtopics.title: Logistics Performance Index
subtopics.summary: The Logistics Performance Index is a World Bank index that analyses differences between countries in customs procedures, logistics costs and infrastructure quality for overland and maritime transport. It is built on six key dimensions and is reported every two years. India ranked 38th among 139 countries in the 2023 report, and the LEADS Index draws inspiration from it.
facts: The LPI analyses differences between countries in customs procedures, logistics costs and quality of infrastructure for overland and maritime transport.
Six key dimensions: Customs Performance, Infrastructure Quality, Ease of Arranging Shipments, Logistics Services Quality, Consignments Tracking and Tracing, and Timeliness of Shipments.
The LPI is reported by the World Bank every 2 years.
India ranked 38th among 139 countries in the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index Report 2023.
The LEADS Index draws inspiration from the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index.

quizzes.title: LEADS Index Check
quizzes.passage: India benchmarks logistics performance through a national index that compares its States and Union Territories with one another. The index draws inspiration from the Logistics Performance Index of the World Bank, an international index that measures logistics performance across countries. States and UTs are evaluated across key logistics parameters, including infrastructure, service quality, the regulatory environment and data-driven logistics reforms. The latest edition of the index introduced a revised performance classification, which replaced the earlier system with new categories for states and UTs. Each state or UT is placed in one of these categories on the basis of its performance across these parameters. Separately, the government recognises excellence and innovation in India's logistics sector through the LEAPS Awards, and the awards were conferred in 2025. The index covers the States and Union Territories of India. The results are presented in a report that was released as the latest edition of the index. Logistics initiatives in India are linked to PM GatiShakti and the National Logistics Policy 2022. Logistics costs in India remain relatively high at around 7.97% of GDP, and the National Logistics Policy 2022 aims to lower them. PM GatiShakti National Master Plan 2021 promotes integrated infrastructure planning across roads, railways, ports, airports and logistics networks.

quizzes.title: Category Recall
quizzes.passage: The LEADS 2025 report places each State and Union Territory into a performance category. Each entry in the report is also marked with a regional group. The regional groups used are coastal, landlocked, north-eastern (N-E) and union territories (UTs). The 2025 edition introduced a new classification system, and its categories are named Exemplars, High Performers, Accelerators and Growth-Seekers. Some states moved up in the 2025 edition after being in earlier categories. For example, a state that had been an Achiever for several years was placed in a new category, and a State or UT that had been a Fast Mover in 2024 moved into a different category in 2025. The LEAPS Awards, which recognise excellence and innovation in India's logistics sector, were also conferred in 2025. The report covers all the States and Union Territories of India, and each one receives a placement based on its performance across logistics parameters such as infrastructure, service quality and the regulatory environment. Parameters also include data-driven logistics reforms, and the index draws inspiration from the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index. Logistics costs in India remain relatively high at around 7.97% of GDP, and the National Logistics Policy 2022 aims to lower them. PM GatiShakti National Master Plan 2021 promotes integrated infrastructure planning.
